5.why: 'reframes rather than reverses' is the sophisticated structure answer; B/D too dismissive, C too specific

6.why: wolves present but no recovery where water low = confound, exactly 'not sufficient'

7.why: weak-Whorf hedged claim (influences speed, doesn't limit); A/B/C are strong-Whorf absolutes

8.why: if the model claims even peripheral birds net a benefit, measured warmth gain supports it; C cuts the other way

9.why: subtle dynamics lost at distance ties the quartets to intimate salon performance, the likely proposal

12.why: disagreement questions turn on the value trade-off, not on facts both sides concede (B, C, D)

21.why: exposing the gap between projected immediacy and deliberate process is the revisionist purpose; C is the surface reading

22.why: recasting an apparent failing as a defensible evidential commitment is the rehabilitation template

23.why: reinterpreting character as construction; C 'defending the common view' is the mirror-image trap

24.why: 'complicates rather than condemns' is the qualifying-final-sentence answer; C reverses, A introduces too much

_pattern_report: Yes, this set felt exploitable, though not on length or position. Length looked deliberately mixed (several long options were obvious distractors, e.g. 3C, 5C, 18B), and my picks spread across letters. The exploitable tell is a shared rhetorical template: on a large fraction of items the credited-looking answer is the hedged, qualified, both-sides claim ('may reassemble', 'without limiting', 'reframes rather than reverses', 'helps normally but fails in severe cases', 'complicates rather than condemns'), while the distractors carry absolutes ('invariably', 'only', 'no role at all', 'regardless', 'all experimental conditions', 'agree'). I answered 5, 7, 13, 16, 17, 18, 22, 23, 24 almost entirely on that concessive/qualified-tone cue. A second, milder tell: many stimuli are recognizable real findings (peacock trains, marshmallow-test reinterpretation, Yellowstone wolves, weak Whorf, junk DNA/ENCODE, Allen's coal-vs-wages thesis, Meiji institutions), so background knowledge substitutes for the passage on 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 16, 20. A candidate coached on 'pick the sophisticated qualified option and dodge extreme words' would beat chance on this batch comfortably without reading a single passage.
